channel.title: FXStreet Forex & Commodities News
channel.description: Real-time Forex News and the latest trading updates. Stay updated on the latest news about currencies and commodities markets.

item.title: Canadian Dollar: Trade dispute weighs on outlook – Commerzbank
item.description: Volkmar Baur at Commerzbank notes that new United States (US) tariffs of 50% on selected Canadian dairy, alcohol and automobile products under Section 338 will remove United States-Mexico-Canada Agreement (USMCA) exemptions.

item.title: Dow Jones futures rise as diplomatic signals ease Middle East tensions
item.description: Dow Jones futures gain 0.29% to trade around 52,220 during European trading hours on Tuesday. Meanwhile, S&P 500 futures and Nasdaq 100 futures advance 0.44% and 1.12%, trading near 7,520 and 29,100, respectively.

item.title: Gold stands firm near one-week high on softer USD; remains below $4,100 amid Fed hike bets
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) hits a one-week high during the first half of the European session on Tuesday, albeit it lacks follow-through buying and remains below the $4,100 mark.

item.title: Indian Rupee: Intervention and inflows counter Brent shock – Societe Generale
item.description: Societe Generale’s Asian FX strategists, including Santosh Ejanthkar and Tanmay Purohit, report that the Indian Rupee (INR) is threatening to retest its record low near 96.9550/USD after Brent crude rose above $90.

item.title: Canadian Dollar recovers from one-week low vs soft USD; lacks bullish conviction
item.description: The USD/CAD pair retreats around 25-30 pips from a one-week high set earlier this Tuesday, and hits a fresh daily low during the first half of the European session.

item.title: Oil: Red Sea route risks and price outlook – MUFG
item.description: MUFG’s Michael Wan notes that disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz have shifted more Middle East Oil flows toward the Red Sea and Bab el-Mandeb, increasing vulnerability to regional conflict.

item.title: UK PM Burnham’s first fiscal policy pledge comes on trial
item.description: A statement from United Kingdom (UK) lawmaker Darren Jones, an ally of former prime minister (PM) Keir Starmer, that the funding source of tax cuts on energy bills, as promised by new PM Andy Burnham, was already unfunded, has pushed political stability optimism under the scanner.

item.title: Japanese Yen weakens against US Dollar despite easing risk aversion
item.description: USD/JPY gains ground for the fourth successive day, trading around 162.60 during the European hours on Tuesday. Japanese banks will be closed due to Marine Day bank holiday.

item.title: Swiss Franc ticks up, but US Dollar dips remain contained amid risk-off markets
item.description: The Swiss Franc (CHF) has trimmed some losses against the US Dollar (USD) on Tuesday, as USD/CHF bulls failed to find acceptance above the 0.8100 area.

item.title: Forex Today: US Dollar struggles to extend rebound as focus remains on Middle East
item.description: Here is what you need to know on Tuesday, July 21:

item.title: Japanese Yen: Pressured within 161.30–163.00 against US Dollar – UOB
item.description: United Overseas Bank’s (UOB) Quek Ser Leang sees USD/JPY holding a firmer tone, with intraday action likely confined to a higher 162.30–162.70 range. Over the next few weeks, a broader consolidation between 161.30 and 163.00 is expected.

item.title: Indian Rupee rebounds as oil prices correct on Mideast peace hopes
item.description: The Indian Rupee (INR) opens higher against the US Dollar on Tuesday. The USD/INR pair corrects to near 96.34 from its two-month high of 96.76 posted on Monday, as fresh hopes of de-escalation in military aggression between the United States (US) and Iran have offered support to the Indian currency.

item.title: Euro rebounds from multi-day low as carry trade undermines JPY; focus remains on ECB
item.description: The EUR/JPY cross attracts some dip-buyers on Tuesday, snapping a three-day losing streak and stalling its recent retracement slide from the 186.00 mark or a nearly one-month high touched last week.

item.title: British Pound: Rally seen fading against Euro – OCBC
item.description: OCBC’s Sim Moh Siong and Christopher Wong flag renewed United Kingdom (UK) fiscal concerns under Prime Minister Andy Burnham as a headwind for the British Pound (GBP).

item.title: AUD/USD Price Forecast: Further upside likely towards 0.7100
item.description: The Australian Dollar (AUD) outperforms its major currency peers, trading 0.28% higher to near 0.7018 against the US Dollar (USD) during the European trading session on Tuesday.

item.title: Euro flatlines above 1.1400 with geopolitical tensions, Oil prices capping rallies
item.description: The Euro (EUR) trades practically flat, a few pips above 1.1400 against the US Dollar (USD) on Tuesday, halfway through the last four weeks horizontal range. A mild reversal on the US Dollar Index has provided some support.

item.title: Equities: Geopolitics weigh on stocks – Deutsche Bank
item.description: Deutsche Bank strategists report the S&P 500 slipping for a third straight session as geopolitical uncertainty and higher US real yields pressure risk assets.

item.title: New Zealand Dollar gathers strength above 0.5850 as CPI inflation data bolster RBNZ rate hike bets
item.description: The NZD/USD pair gains traction to around 0.5860 during the early European trading hours on Tuesday. Hotter New Zealand inflation data provide some support to the New Zealand Dollar (NZD) against the US Dollar (USD). The US ADP Employment report will be published later on Tuesday.

item.title: Brent: Geopolitics weigh on prices – ING
item.description: ING strategists Warren Patterson and Ewa Manthey note Brent retreated below $90/bbl as hopes for US–Iran de-escalation offset rising supply risks. They highlight reports of a proposed 10‑day ceasefire and ongoing large divisions between the US and Iran.

item.title: Euro pulls back against a stronger Pound following upbeat UK employment data
item.description: The Euro (EUR) posts moderate losses against the British Pound (GBP) on Tuesday, yet trading within recent ranges.

item.title: US Dollar: Fed inflation framework questions – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank’s Volkmar Baur discusses how persistent high Oil and energy prices complicate the Federal Reserve’s stance, with markets only modestly pricing in further tightening.

item.title: British Pound attracts bids after UK employment data release
item.description: The British Pound (GBP) snaps a three-day losing streak against the Japanese Yen (JPY), rebounding to near 218.55 during the European trading session on Tuesday. The cross attracts bids after the release of the United Kingdom (UK) labor market data for the three months ending May.

item.title: British Pound holds positive ground near 1.3450 after UK employment data
item.description: The GBP/USD pair holds positive ground near 1.3450 during the early European trading hours on Tuesday. The British Pound (GBP) strengthens against the US Dollar (USD) following the UK employment report.

item.title: Euro: Downward bias capped by 1.1390 support against US Dollar – UOB
item.description: United Overseas Bank’s (UOB) Quek Ser Leang sees EUR/USD retaining a mild downside bias after slipping below a prior strong support at 1.1405. Intraday losses are expected to be limited to tests of 1.1390, with resistance at 1.1430–1.1445.

item.title: UK Unemployment Rate steadies at 4.9% in May vs. 5.0% expected
item.description: The United Kingdom’s (UK) ILO Unemployment Rate remained steady at 4.9% in the three months to May after reporting 4.9% in the previous reading, data published by the Office for National Statistics (ONS) showed on Tuesday. The data came in below the market consensus of 5.0%.

item.title: Silver Price Forecast: XAG/USD surges to near $58.20 as oil price rally hits pause
item.description: Silver price (XAG/USD) is up over 3% to near $58.20 during the early European trading session on Tuesday.

item.title: EUR/JPY Price Forecast: Holds gains above 185.50 near nine-day EMA support
item.description: EUR/JPY edges higher after three days of losses, trading around 185.50 during the Asian hours on Tuesday. The currency cross is holding above both the nine-day and 50-day Exponential Moving Averages (EMAs), which reinforces a mildly bullish near-term bias.

item.title: WTI declines toward $82.00 as traders digest US-Iran developments
item.description: West Texas Intermediate (WTI), the US crude oil benchmark, is trading around $82.00 during the early European trading hours on Tuesday. The WTI declines but remains near multi-week highs as traders continue to assess the developments surrounding the US-Iran conflicts.

item.title: USD/CAD Price Forecast: Intraday positive move stalls ahead of 1.4100 confluence hurdle
item.description: The USD/CAD pair attracts buyers for the second straight day on Tuesday and recovers further from its lowest level since June 17, around the 1.4000 psychological mark touched the previous day.

item.title: Iran’s IRGC says it hit US military targets in Bahrain and Kuwait
item.description: The Iranian Islamic Revolutionary Guards Corps (IRGC) said that it struck US military targets, including air defence systems in Bahrain and Kuwait, the Guardian reported on Tuesday.
